note: WORLD DENSITY levels (game.WorldDensity; the GAME tab's 'World density', the HOST's choice in co-op and the same for every peer). One row per level -- change a number here to tune a level, nothing else. traffic = simulated ambient cars (ZoneManager.trafficBudget; game/traffic.json scales it per region), walkers = crowd pedestrians promoted to full bodies at once, fighters = how many of those may fight, attack_tokens = units added to crimes.json / gangs.json tokens_by_stars at every star level that has a limit (how many may attack one player at once). body_cap = the island-wide ceiling on ENFORCEMENT bodies -- police, gang hunters, incident responders, car and helicopter crews together (EnforcementDispatch.bodyCap, PLAN.md P1e; 0 = no cap). 48 / 60 / 72 are UNMEASURED picks (2026-10-15): measure with probe_walk_perf -- --density=<LEVEL> --wanted=5 --gang=5 and set the shipped number here; a host or a tester overrides it without touching this file (user://overrides/density.json, see util.DataTable.overridesIn). NORMAL is the baseline: 20 cars since 2026-10-10 late (user: 'at least stable around 12 cars most of the time, even if it means fewer peds' -- 20 in the 210 m ring is ~15 within 200 m and ~5 within 100 m of a player). It is paid for by trafficLazyDrivers, not by peds: a car on rails carries no driver body, and measured (probe_walk_perf, two downtown legs, physics ms per frame p95) 20 such cars cost 13.6 / 16.5 against 18.8 / 19.8 for the old 12 cars with a driver each; 28 cost 14.7 / 19.0. NOT measured on a Steam Deck, and the draw-call side was not measurable on this machine's software renderer. Run a session or a probe at a level with OW_WORLD_DENSITY=HIGH (or probe_walk_perf -- --density=HIGH).
